Small update to **Nexo** that fixes low frame rates when streaming games. If you're on v0.2.0-alpha.1,
Nexo updates itself. Look for the **Restart to update** banner.

## Fixes

- **Smoother game streams on Windows.** Screen shares now use your GPU's hardware video encoder
  (NVIDIA NVENC, AMD AMF, Intel Quick Sync) instead of a software encoder. This frees up your CPU while
  you play.
- **Low-fps hint.** If your stream drops to a few fps while the game has focus, the game is running with
  an **uncapped frame rate**. It saturates the GPU and Windows can't capture the screen in time. Nexo
  now detects this and tells you. **Cap the game's FPS** (V-Sync, an in-game max FPS setting, or the GPU
  control panel). Any cap fixes it.
- The voice panel now shows your stream's live fps. Hover it to see the resolution, the encoder, and
  whether bandwidth is limiting the stream.

## Install

New here? Download the file for your system from the **Assets** below. The installers are **not
code-signed**, so your OS will warn you the first time.

- **Windows:** run `Nexo-Setup-<version>.exe`. If SmartScreen says "Windows protected your PC", click
  **More info → Run anyway**.
- **macOS:** open the `.dmg` and drag Nexo to **Applications**. The first time, **right-click Nexo →
  Open → Open**. If macOS says the app "is damaged", run `xattr -cr /Applications/Nexo.app` in Terminal.
- **Linux:** `chmod +x Nexo-*.AppImage && ./Nexo-*.AppImage`.

Coming from **v0.1.0-alpha.1**? That version can't update itself, so install this one by hand once.

No server changes: hosts don't need to update anything.
